clue.text: It made dress stand out in the hurly-burly

definitions.meaning: a padded frame worn under the back of a Victorian skirt to make it puff out

explanation.surface: Something that made a dress stand out amid all the commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the padded skirt support and a scene of busy, fussy activity.

clue.text: Consecutive houses may be built in this fashion

definitions.meaning: one straight after another, in unbroken succession

definitions.text: houses may be built in this fashion
definitions.meaning: terraced homes sharing a rear wall with the row behind, common in northern English industrial towns

explanation.surface: Houses in a row built one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in succession and also describes rows of houses sharing their rear walls.

clue.text: A year and a day for lecher

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday
yr is the standard abbreviation for a year

explanation.surface: Someone takes a year and a day off to pursue a lecher.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the goat-legged woodland spirit was famously lustful, so the name is used for a lustful man.

clue.text: Short member of RAF obtains an honour

parts.note: LAC is a Leading Aircraftman, a rank in the Royal Air Force
in bridge the king is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: A minor airman in the Royal Air Force receives an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like part of the airman's description, but it is the definition; the honour is a bridge card, not a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of something means wanting or missing it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Bill and Paul resolved to join firm in Mexican resort

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and reformed, so the name Paul is rearranged

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Paul decide to join a company in a Mexican holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific coast city in Mexico is a well-known beach holiday destination.

clue.text: Depression when senior officer is given a medal

parts.note: CO is a Commanding Officer
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A commander becomes gloomy despite being awarded a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood; it is a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short valley or hollow, a depression in the land.

clue.text: It's impolitic travelling without it in this district of London

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of impolitic move about

parts.note: taken as written, the letters left over from the rearrangement

explanation.surface: It is unwise to drive through this part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IMPOLITIC with the letters of IT taken away ('without it').
explanation.definitionFit: Pimlico is a residential area of central London near Victoria.

clue.text: When to take a short break in Munich, let loose

definitions.text: When to take a short break

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters of Munich and let are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for a quick holiday in Munich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short break' looks like a trip; it is the midday meal pause.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal break is a short pause in the working day.

clue.text: Do what you're told round governor

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: Follow orders from the governor.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with instructions is to do as one is told.

clue.text: In the event, get a severe punishment

definitions.meaning: an athletics field event in which competitors leap over a raised bar
from the idiom 'for the ...', in serious trouble

explanation.surface: During the competition, someone is heavily penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is an athletics discipline and, in British idiom, a looming severe punishment.

clue.text: Questions in schematic arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of schematic gives a new word

explanation.surface: A set of questions laid out in a diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious teaching text arranged as questions and answers.

clue.text: Aquatic creature with fur, white at the tail

parts.note: mink is a valuable fur

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A sea animal with fur that turns white at its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A minke is a small baleen whale, an animal living in water.

clue.text: Confection giving pleasure in Istanbul

definitions.meaning: a sweet made of gel dusted with sugar
read literally, joy felt in Turkey's biggest city

explanation.surface: A sweet that brings joy in Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet's name, read word by word, means a Turkish pleasure.

clue.text: A mound of calcium carbonate prison has me eating it

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other, the letters of me around it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner complains that the camp has them eating chalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is a column of mineral deposit rising from a cave floor.

clue.text: Escort vessel without a name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ship surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An unnamed ship escorts others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone is to accompany or escort them along.

clue.text: Pretend one girl is holding a drink

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: is holding means the name contains the drink

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a gin, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone pretends a girl is clutching a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend, as an adjective, means make-believe or not real.

clue.text: Unfortunately golf is out for someone into spacecraft

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Golf is cancelled, sadly, for a space enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies unidentified flying objects is interested in alien spacecraft.

clue.text: Tax finished with approval, when return's first entered

parts.note: over means ended

indicators.note: entered means the letter goes inside the approval

parts.note: OK signals approval

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of return

explanation.surface: Tax paperwork finished and approved once the return was filed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to burden or overwork them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sign spotted once, Pennies off sour fruit

parts.note: the Crab is Cancer, a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: off in the sense of removed or knocked off, so the pennies are taken out of the spotted word

parts.note: dappled means marked with spots
d was the symbol for an old British penny, so two of them

explanation.surface: A star sign once spotted pennies falling off sour fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' points to pre-decimal British money, where d stood for a penny; remove both Ds from DAPPLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild apple with very sharp-tasting flesh.

clue.text: Hold wife off wizard embracing maiden

indicators.note: off in the sense of sent away or removed, so the wife's letter is dropped from the wizard
embracing means the wizard surrounds the maiden

parts.note: a warlock is a male witch or wizard
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A wizard hugs a girl while keeping his wife away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is a wrestling grip; 'embracing' puts M inside the wizard before the W goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm lock is a grip used in wrestling, a hold.

clue.text: Expression of delight by one who's a novice — at this?

definitions.text: Expression of delight by one who's a novice — at this?

parts.note: whee is a cry of joy
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A learner driver cries out in delight behind the steering.
explanation.walkthrough: A learner driver is 'at the wheel'; the whole clue works as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The steering control is what a novice driver sits at, crying out happily.

clue.text: A rather unscrupulous person Tweedledum, for instance

definitions.meaning: a sharp, dodgy dealer, British slang
read literally, a broad, fat lad like Lewis Carroll's rotund twin

explanation.surface: A shady character, such as Tweedledum.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a petty crook, and literally a broad boy like the rotund twin.

clue.text: Ice kind of cake for this celebration

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a wedding cake

explanation.surface: Icing a special cake for a big party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' looks like a verb about icing a cake; it is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixtieth anniversary of marriage is celebrated with this name.

clue.text: Time for bed? It's almost time

parts.note: nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: Is it bedtime? It's nearly time.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours are when people go to sleep.

clue.text: Cove's home rented

parts.note: at home means in
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A man's house is rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' reads as British slang for a man; it is a small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cove is a small sheltered bay, a narrow arm of water.

clue.text: Insect's initially flexible joint, perhaps

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of flexible

explanation.surface: An insect has an initially flexible joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat may be cut from cattle, an example of the type.

clue.text: Time to muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time to think deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb, but it is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Muse of love poetry is one of the nine.

clue.text: Biscuit that's good: a blue one

parts.note: blue in the sense of risque or crude, like a dirty joke
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A good biscuit cheers up a sad person.
explanation.definitionFit: A British biscuit containing a layer of squashed currants.

clue.text: I felt unhappy about foolish talk to test public opinion

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the talk
unhappy letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: yak means idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone feels miserable about silly chatter while gauging opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' turns I FELT into FLITE, around YAK.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means float an idea to see how people react.

clue.text: Attempt to get into tree, backing into shrub

indicators.note: backing means the combined letters are read from end to start
to get into means the attempt is placed inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to climb a tree, then retreating into the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' makes ELTRYM, which 'backing' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.
